report:
## Conclusion

Your view is supported: **there is no reliable evidence that soursop (also called graviola; *Annona muricata*) cures cancer in humans.** It should not replace evidence-based cancer care.

**Why laboratory findings do not establish a cure:** Soursop extracts and acetogenins can kill or slow cancer cells in cell-culture experiments, and some animal research is promising. But this is preliminary evidence: substances that harm isolated cancer cells can also harm normal cells, may not reach tumors safely in people, and frequently fail in human trials. The NCI-indexed pancreatic-cancer paper, for example, explicitly concerns *in vitro* and animal work—not cancer outcomes in patients.  
https://edrn.cancer.gov/data-and-resources/publications/22475682-2053-graviola-a-novel-promising-natural-derived-drug-that-inhibits-tumorigenicity-and-metastasis-of-pancreatic-cancer-cells-in-vitro-and-in-vivo-through-altering-cell-metabolism/

**What human evidence shows:** Cancer Research UK states there is not enough reliable evidence that graviola works as a cancer treatment. A recent systematic review specifically set out to compile human cancer evidence, underscoring how limited this evidence base is; it does not establish a cure.  
https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/about-cancer/treatment/complementary-alternative-therapies/individual-therapies/graviola  
https://mjpharm.org/effect-of-annona-muricata-soursop-on-patients-with-cancer-a-systematic-review/

**Safety matters:** “Natural” does not mean safe. Compounds in soursop (acetogenins) have raised neurotoxicity concerns, including possible links to atypical parkinsonism. Memorial Sloan Kettering likewise notes that clinical evidence for its cancer use is lacking. Supplements can vary greatly in dose and composition and may interact with treatment.

Bottom line: it is reasonable to eat the fruit as food if medically appropriate, but claims that it **cures** cancer are unsupported. A person with cancer should discuss any soursop product with their oncology team and should not delay or stop prescribed treatment.  
https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/graviola
